# libmirisdr4

**Open driver for Mirics-based receivers, including SDRplay RSP hardware**

- **Version recorded:** 2.0.0
- **Categories:** `sdr-hardware`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/f4exb/libmirisdr-4>

## What it does

A free-software driver for receivers built on Mirics silicon, which includes the SDRplay RSP line, plus the udev rules for them.

## Why you would want it

It is the open alternative to SDRplay's proprietary API, so RSP hardware can be used without a closed binary driver. It is also the source of the identifiers in the sdrplay-rsp hardware entry.

## Before it will work

Mirics-based hardware.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install libmirisdr4 --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `libmirisdr4`

## Known problems

It does not implement everything SDRplay's own API does, and current RSP models may enumerate differently from what this driver recognises — the sdrplay-rsp entry records that gap rather than assuming it away. Naming trap: the package is libmirisdr4, not libmirisdr0, which older documentation cites.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
